messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis  
Details:  
The failing test `testExistingFilePattern` verifies that parsing an option with the pattern "g<" correctly produces a `FileInputStream` option object when parsing a file path argument. The "g<" pattern means that option "g" has an argument with type `EXISTING_FILE_VALUE`, defined in `PatternOptionBuilder` as `FileInputStream.class`. This indicates that the parsed option value should be a `FileInputStream`.  

The `PatternOptionBuilder.parsePattern` method processes the pattern string "g<". It recognizes 'g' as the option character and '<' as a value code corresponding to the type `EXISTING_FILE_VALUE` (`FileInputStream.class`). It builds an option with `.hasArg(true)` and type set to `FileInputStream.class`.  

The `DefaultParser.parse` method reads the option arguments and processes tokens. When an option expects an argument, it stores the string argument value using `Option.addValueForProcessing`, which calls `processValue` internally on the option to convert the string argument into the typed object expected.  

The bug report states that the option parser type `EXISTING_FILE_VALUE` does not check whether the file actually exists before returning the `FileInputStream`. This behavior means that although the code assigns type `FileInputStream` to the option, it may not perform a check ensuring the passed file path exists and is readable before creating the stream.  

The test uses a file path "src/test/resources/existing-readable.file" which exists, expecting the parsed option object to be a `FileInputStream`. If the implementation does not check for file existence, it may incorrectly parse non-existing files or behave unexpectedly. The root cause lies in the option value conversion code (likely in the option or parser's processValue method) where the conversion from the string filename to the `FileInputStream` object is done without a file existence check. This violates the expectation for `EXISTING_FILE_VALUE` type options: that the file must exist and be readable before creating the stream.  

No recent bug reports indicate related fixes. The core issue is that the `EXISTING_FILE_VALUE` option type conversion does not validate file existence before returning the `FileInputStream`. This causes the test to fail or could cause erroneous behavior in production code relying on this type.  

The fix should be located in the path where the string argument is converted to the typed object for the option, presumably in the `Option` class's value processing or elsewhere in `DefaultParser`. There should be a check before creating a `FileInputStream` that the file exists and is accessible.  

This diagnosis matches both the test and current bug report: the bug is that the `EXISTING_FILE_VALUE` type is not fully validated when parsing the command line option to the expected `FileInputStream` type.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
